standard_prerequisites.name: Delta_0-completeness in Q
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every Delta_0 formula B(x) and every n, if N satisfies B(numeral n) then Q proves B(numeral n).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the cited engine of the proof (2113-2117); it is the unit's own lemma lem:delta0-completeness.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sigma_1 form
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Sigma_1 sentence is a sentence of the form exists x A(x) with A a Delta_0 formula.
standard_prerequisites.use: It fixes the shape of the sentence the proof analyzes (2106-2110).

core_obligations: Witness extraction: truth in N of exists x A(x) gives a natural number n and an assignment s with s(x)=n and N satisfies A(x)[s] (2107-2111).
Substitution fact for satisfaction: N satisfies A(x)[s] iff N satisfies A(numeral n) (2111-2113).
A(numeral n) is Delta_0, so by Delta_0-completeness Q proves A(numeral n), and existential generalization yields Q proves exists x A(x) (2113-2118).

proof_roadmap.step: Extract the witnessing number and assignment from truth in N.
Convert the satisfaction fact to the substituted instance.

difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the author theorem at source lines 2100-2104: if A is a Sigma_1 sentence true in the standard model N, then Q proves A. The author proof (2106-2118) is complete: a true Sigma_1 sentence exists x A(x) yields a witnessing natural number n and assignment with s(x)=n and N satisfies A(x) under s; the substitution fact for the satisfaction relation converts this to N satisfying A(numeral n); A(numeral n) is Delta_0, so the unit's Delta_0-completeness lemma gives Q proves A(numeral n); existential generalization finishes. The only invoked external result is the unit's own Delta_0-completeness lemma, cited by label and separately proved.
